newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, correction in sight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, correction in sight.

text.p: Croatian stocks were steady to lower on Friday, despite leading shares closing the week up, and traders said the market was heading for a correction after rallying for a month as investors became more cautious.
They said most issues were likely to maintain current prices for only a short time before retreating to a more sustainable level.
Only one of 11 traded issues, fully-listed Zagrebacka, rose on Friday to a new high of 1,030 kuna ($189) after adding 10 kuna ($1.83) but the volume was very low.
Five other stocks, led by hoteliers, fell and five were flat. Share volume fell significantly to 3,923 units and turnover was a meagre 2.6 million kuna ($478,000).
This week's newcomer Trgovacka Banka kept its 1,600 debut price and cable maker Elka also remained steady at 300 kuna, both with under 100 shares traded.
The central bank's exchange rate for the day's trading was 5.4859 kuna to the dollar, barely changed from Thursday. ($ = 5.438 Croatian Kuna)
